summary.name: SaneBar
summary.one_liner: A free, open source (MIT) macOS menu bar manager that hides and reveals menu bar icons, with optional Touch ID or password lock.
keywords: menu bar icons disappear behind notch
use_cases: Decluttering a crowded macOS menu bar
Recovering icons hidden behind the MacBook notch
Locking hidden menu bar icons with Touch ID or a password
Auto-revealing icons on low battery, Wi-Fi, Focus or app launch
Migrating from Bartender or Ice to a free open source tool
summary.what_it_does: SaneBar hides menu bar apps you do not need right now and keeps important ones visible. Clicking its icon or using the ⌘\ shortcut reveals or hides the icons. Hidden icons can be browsed in a floating Icon Panel or a full-width Second Menu Bar, where you can search by name and double-click to open an app. It offers Visible, Hidden and Always Hidden zones, icon groups, and drag between zones. Smart triggers, profiles, appearance controls, per-icon hotkeys and AppleScript/Shortcuts automation are included. The page says all features are free and on-device by default.
notable: Free and fully open source under MIT license, with every feature unlocked and no license key
Touch ID and password lock for hidden icons
Smart triggers (battery, Wi-Fi, Focus, app launch, schedule, script) and AppleScript/Shortcuts automation
Imports layouts and settings from Bartender or Ice
caveats: Page says SaneBar cannot hide icons on macOS 27
Requires macOS Accessibility permission to hide, reveal and move menu bar items
A small number of unusual menu bar apps may be edge cases and not work well
